name: Pilot and field watch
summary: The legible tool watch for the cockpit and the field. It has a steel case, a matt black dial with large white luminous numerals, a large crown for gloves and a long strap. The Hour Angle watch of 1931 and the German observation watches of the 1930s set the type.

philosophy.core_thesis: A tool watch must be read at a glance, in poor light and with a glove on. Each part serves legibility and nothing else.
design_principles: Print white Arabic numerals on a matt black dial, and mark the 12 with a triangle and two dots.
Cut the hands as bold batons or swords filled with luminous paint, and make the minute hand reach the track.
Make the crown 7 to 9 mm wide, as an onion or a fluted wheel, so that a gloved hand can wind it.
Make a field watch 34 to 38 mm wide, and a pilot's watch 40 to 55 mm wide that goes over a flight sleeve.
Fit a soft-iron cage round the movement, so that the magnetic fields of aircraft instruments cannot move the balance.
Keep the dial matt, so that the glare stays low in a cockpit.
Cut the strap 200 to 250 mm long, so that it goes over a flight jacket, and rivet it to the lugs.
Leave the dial free of ornament, logos and extra scales.
anti_patterns: Small numerals and thin hands that do not glow
A mirror-polished case that flashes in the sun
A dial that is crowded with sub dials and windows
A thin dress case that a knock can bend
A short strap that fits only a bare wrist

silhouette.shape: A round steel case, small for a field watch and large for a pilot's watch, with a big crown and a plain bezel.
silhouette.line: A plain circle with short lugs, a thin bezel and a crown that stands clear of the case.
silhouette.fit: The strap wraps the wrist or goes over a sleeve, and the dial faces the user without a tilt.
silhouette.proportion: Case thickness to width is about 1 to 3.5. The dial fills about 85 per cent of the case. The numerals are 4 to 6 mm tall.
rules: Make the dial the largest part of the face and keep the bezel narrow.
Set the 12 triangle at the top and keep the other numerals the same size.
Make the minute hand longer than the hour hand by at least 3 mm.
Leave the crown free of guards so that a glove can grip the crown.

fabrics.rule: Use steel for the case, matt black for the dial and luminous paint for the glow. Put the watch on leather, canvas or nylon webbing.

methods: luminous paint on numerals and hands
construction.closures: A buckle closes a long strap; a large fluted or onion crown winds and sets the watch.
construction.details: A triangle at 12 with two dots, large baton hands, a long strap and a crown wide enough for a glove.

surface.pattern: A matt black dial with white numerals and a minute track; no ornament.
surface.gloss: Brushed steel at 15 to 40 GU; the dial at 2 to 5 GU; the crystal at 90 GU.
surface.wear: The steel scratches to a soft grey, the luminous paint yellows, the canvas fades and the leather darkens; wear is part of the look.

palette.strategy: Black and white for reading, steel for the case, and the green and brown of the field for the strap.

processes: dial printing in white on black
making.scale: Factory output for air forces and armies in lots of thousands; each maker met one military specification.
making.signs: A triangle at 12, a large crown, white on black and a long strap.

emotion.target_response: A calm readiness: the viewer sees a plain face that works at a glance, in poor light and with a glove.

use_cases: a prop for an air war or an expedition film
an image prompt for a field watch on canvas
avoid_when: the brief wants a dress watch
the brief wants gold, diamonds or enamel
the brief wants a function for the sea or for timing

modifiers.how: Thicken the case, add a rotating bezel and a screw-down crown, and rate the case for 100 m or more.
Add two chronograph pushers, a tachymeter ring and sub dials, and keep the black dial.
